qas.question: During the hospitalization from 2132-06-30 to 2132-07-08, what combination of findings made the team treat this as a catheter-related bloodstream infection despite the patient’s low white blood cell count?

qas.question: During the hospitalization from 2132-06-30 to 2132-07-08, why did the doctor argue that removing the right femoral tunneled catheter was the safest step rather than trying to salvage it?

qas.question: During the hospitalization from 2132-06-30 to 2132-07-08, how did the CT abdomen/pelvis result change the interpretation of the patient’s lower abdominal pain?

qas.question: During the hospitalization from 2132-06-30 to 2132-07-08, what was the sequence of dialysis access changes from admission through discharge planning?

qas.question: During the hospitalization from 2132-06-30 to 2132-07-08, what did the echocardiogram result imply about the MRSA infection’s spread, and how did it affect treatment duration?

qas.question: During the hospitalization from 2132-06-30 to 2132-07-08, why did the team pursue central venous evaluation and later IVC angioplasty even after leg ultrasounds showed no DVT?

qas.question: During the hospitalization from 2132-06-30 to 2132-07-08, why was vancomycin continued as the sole targeted antibiotic after initially adding broader coverage?

qas.question: During the hospitalization from 2132-06-30 to 2132-07-08, what did the negative pelvic infectious testing imply about the cause of ongoing vaginal discharge, and what follow-up was recommended?

qas.question: During the hospitalization from 2132-06-30 to 2132-07-08, why did the team send Strongyloides antibody testing in the setting of persistent eosinophilia?
